answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a node’s weight is the probability mass reaching it from trusted seeds. A sybil cluster typically forms a sparse external cut, so its low conductance limits escape and caps imported mass; min-cut transitivity bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, preventing colluding identities from amplifying influence. This remains true across a voyage, mesa, or nebula of attestations.
